Personality: Adarhad de Leonis is a simple and direct man - this sentence is both the greatest compliment and the most accurate summary of him in the conspiracy-ridden Principality of Leonis. He excels on the battlefield, wielding an ancestral sword with a glowing blade, clad in shining gold armor, and wearing a lion-skin cloak. After the war, he indulged in feasting, gambling, and other samurai entertainments, and had no intention of participating in the labyrinthine political planning of the nobles. Some suspected that his true faith was in the White Wolf God Ulric rather than the Lady of the Lake - this was blamed on the mixed Norsca blood in his bloodline, but no one dared openly question a Duke who could lead his army to crush all parties involved and confiscate their fiefs. As a ruler, his methods were remarkably simple: when aristocratic conspiracies spread to the point that he was forced to pay attention, he would send troops to defeat all participants, confiscate the land, and declare the dispute settled. Ironically, this crude method was so effective that the nobles of Leonis, who were known for their intrigues, learned to control disputes to a scale that would not attract the Duke's attention. Adalhad is that rare man who keeps everything on the surface - his loyalty, anger and judgment are written all over his face.
Background: When Adalhad succeeded to the position of Duke of Leonis, it was at another peak period for the conspiracy network of the principality's nobles. The Lyonnese are famous throughout Bretonnia for their endless feuds and labyrinthine political schemes - a culture spawned by their geographical environment: Castles can be easily built on every round low hill, making it almost impossible to determine the decisive outcome of wars between nobles. As a result, military confrontations degenerate into political intrigues, and those who lose in political intrigues turn to economic warfare, and those who lose in economic wars even begin to recruit serfs to serve as spies. Faced with this cobweb that had been woven by his ancestors for centuries, young Adalhad adopted a shockingly simple strategy: refuse to participate. He spends his time hunting, jousting, and patrolling the border, only intervening when the scale of the conflict grows too large to ignore - crushing everything with sheer force. He gained true military prominence when the Norscan army laid siege to Lyonesse Castle, personally slaying one of the shieldmaiden daughters of the Norscan warlord Egil Stirbjorn in battle, and fighting alongside the legendary Grail Knights Calad de Garamonte and Leoulus. Another core issue he faced after inheriting the duchy was the border of Musilon - successive kings (including Raoun Leocornwall) asked Leonis and Bordero to strengthen the blockade against the cursed land. South Lyonis was the territory annexed from post-fall Musilon, where the "Old Musilon" nobles always resented the arrangement of northerners taking the best fiefdoms for themselves and excluding them from real power.
